text:
sachin: quick heads-up — scheduled cutover tonight at 00:30 UTC (prod-wave-7). deploy-bot has the window. We need API/runtime/console/router owners to ack pins and rollback plan. @maria @zhang @dion

deploy-bot: Deploy window reserved: 2026-03-21T00:30Z -> 2026-03-21T01:30Z. Canary plan: 5% for 10m -> 25% for 15m -> 100%. Auto-rollback triggers: error rate >5% for 5m OR p50 latency >200ms for 10m.

sachin: Current pins I'm planning to push in release metadata: api=v2.1.3, runtime=v3.0.0-rc4, console=no-change, router=v1.9.1. If anyone needs a different pin, speak now. Also need explicit owner for step 3 (runtime image revert).

maria: ack for runtime pin. i'll be oncall 00:15-01:00. if we hit regressions we revert runtime to runtime:v2.9 (we validated warm cache flows).

zhang: router ack. i'll keep header-swap disabled until after 25% stage. will run pin/rollback commands if needed.

dion: console ack. only a small feature flag behind server-side flag — safe. i'll push a short release note blurb and update postmortem template if we roll back.

sachin: good. writing steps into release notes now. Proposed rollback steps (one-button sequence we can run manually):
1) abort canary / stop traffic shift (router)
2) pin router version back to previous stable
3) promote runtime image to runtime:v2.9 (maria)
4) demote API to v2.1.2 if errors persist
5) open incident & notify customers if >30m outage

maria: i got step 3. tested rollback in staging. command we'll use:
```
kubectl -n prod set image deployment/runtime runtime=ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:v2.9
```
I'll prep the image tag and have it staged in container registry.

zhang: router pin command (ready):
```
routerctl pin --service=router --version=v1.9.0 --reason="rollback to stable"
```
I'll stand by at deploy start.

deploy-bot: Canary started: prod-wave-7 canary=5% (00:30:00 UTC). Monitoring metrics: errors, p50/p95 latency, memory OOMs.

(00:40 UTC) deploy-bot: Alert — canary errors 6.1% over 5m; p50 latency 240ms. condition: error_rate >5% -> firing

maria: :eyes: i see the same on runtime traces (increased KV fetch times). initiating rollback step 3 now.

zhang: holding traffic. pinning router to v1.9.0 in 1m.

dion: updating release notes and support slack. quick note: "Rolled back tonight due to latency regression in runtime affecting API p50". Will post short statement to #support.

sachin: do it. maria, run the kubectl command and report when image replaced. zhang, confirm pin done.

maria: running: `kubectl -n prod set image deployment/runtime runtime=ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:v2.9` -> image pull started.

deploy-bot: Router pinned: router=v1.9.0 by zhang at 00:42:30 UTC.

maria: runtime rollout complete: new pods up with v2.9, readiness OK. CPU steady.

deploy-bot: Canary aborted and traffic reverted to baseline. Canary wave marked ROLLBACK by sachin. Metrics rolling back to baseline.

sachin: excellent — thanks everyone. follow-ups:
- dion, add a line to release notes explaining regression root cause as "KV latency rise with rc4 kernel path"
- maria, please capture kernel traces and open an internal bug linking runtime PR and the canary metrics
- zhang, leave router pinned until we validate 24h stable

dion: will update release notes and ping #support. draft: "Deployment to prod halted and rolled back due to increased runtime latency impacting API p50; team reverted runtime to last stable while we investigate."

maria: opened bug: BUG-2147 with traces + perf graphs. cc: runtime-team.

zhang: router left pinned v1.9.0. will unpin after ops signoff.

sachin: closing the wave as ROLLED_BACK. we'll reschedule a follow-up RFC for the runtime last-to-merge gating. thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Wave summary: prod-wave-7 -> ROLLED_BACK at 00:44:12 UTC. Canary duration: ~14m. Trigger: runtime latency >200ms and error rate >5%. Operators involved: sachin, maria, zhang, dion.

maria: quick retrospective note — we should add a short preflight: `lite-kernel-smoke` for rc kernels in dedicated canary lane. saves a rollback later.

sachin: agreed. adding to next week's release retro.

(END)
